description: An HR director must finalize a restorative response to a complaint that a project lead repeatedly shut a colleague out of team discussions. The decision must set the response type, incident record, communication boundaries, coaching, and management follow-up.

shared_context.S1: Leila has complained that Marcus repeatedly interrupts or redirects her during meetings for the customer-transition project.
shared_context.S2: Marcus leads the project, and Renee manages both Marcus and Leila.
shared_context.S3: The project has two recurring working meetings each week, and the next meeting is scheduled for Monday.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the binding HR decision; before closing the matter, the normal review process gives the complainant, respondent, observing colleague, and department manager a separate, uninterrupted opportunity to state what the resolution should address.
shared_context.S5: Each participant must put any firsthand observation, prior agreement, promise, or personal condition that is not already in the case record on the record through a reveal action before Elena makes the decision; a general proposal or acknowledgment does not substitute for revealing that underlying fact.
shared_context.S6: Elena waits until all four participants have had that opportunity and asks anyone who has not yet made a reveal to do so before accepting a settlement.

PF1.text: Leila told a trusted colleague that she will participate in a repair meeting only if future project coordination uses a shared written channel and agendas are sent at least 24 hours in advance; she has not yet stated this condition directly to Elena because she feared being labeled difficult.

PF2.text: Marcus agreed in his most recent one-to-one with Renee to complete a six-week communication-coaching plan with a Wednesday session each week, but that agreement was not attached to Elena's complaint file.

PF3.text: Tobias personally observed exactly four meetings in which Marcus interrupted Leila and then reassigned her question to someone else; he has not submitted a written witness account because he expected management to handle the matter informally.

PF4.text: Renee promised Leila that she would attend the first three joint project meetings after any repair process and hold a private weekly check-in with Leila for four weeks, but she has not recorded that promise in the case notes.

acceptance_conditions: The response must be a restorative or facilitative process that includes a repair meeting rather than a punitive warning.
The case record must state exactly four qualifying incidents.
A facilitated repair meeting must be required.
Project coordination must use a shared written channel.
Meeting agendas must be provided at least 24 hours in advance.
Marcus must have a six-week communication-coaching commitment with sessions on Wednesdays.
Renee must attend the first three joint project meetings and hold weekly private check-ins with Leila for four weeks.

content_checks.C1: decisions['incident_count_recorded'] == 4 and decisions['repair_meeting_required'] == True and decisions['response_type'] in ['restorative_developmental', 'restorative', 'facilitative_resolution', 'Formal resolution with facilitated repair meeting and structural meeting modifications', 'Coaching and procedural reform with facilitated repair meeting', 'Facilitative resolution with binding commitments and managerial oversight', 'coaching and process changes']
content_checks.C4: decisions['communication_channel'] in ['shared_written_channel', 'Shared written channel for all project coordination', 'Shared written project coordination channel', 'Shared written channel for all project coordination, decisions, action items, and discussion points', 'shared written project coordination channel'] and decisions['agenda_notice_hours'] >= 24
content_checks.C6: any(c['target'] == 'Marcus' and c['type'] in ['coaching', 'communication_coaching'] for c in commitments) and decisions['coaching_plan_weeks'] == 6 and decisions['coaching_day'] in ['Wednesday', 'wednesdays']
content_checks.C7: any(c['target'] == 'Renee' and c['type'] in ['manager_attendance', 'manager_oversight', 'managerial oversight commitment'] for c in commitments) and decisions['manager_attendance_meetings'] == 3
content_checks.C8: any(c['target'] == 'Renee' and c['type'] in ['weekly_checkin', 'private_check_ins', 'manager_oversight', 'managerial oversight commitment'] for c in commitments) and decisions['manager_checkin_weeks'] == 4

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: Leila's condition changes the communication channel to a shared written channel and fixes the agenda-notice threshold at exactly 24 hours.
Marcus's prior agreement changes the support plan to a six-week communication-coaching plan with one session each Wednesday.
Tobias's firsthand account changes the incident record to exactly four meetings and supports a restorative response requiring a facilitated repair meeting.
Renee's prior promise changes management follow-up to attendance at exactly the first three joint meetings and private weekly check-ins for exactly four weeks.
